Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04 16:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lina Gomez (Redwood SE), Karen Cho (Mosaic CTO), Miguel Alvarez (Mosaic ML Eng), Rita Singh (Product)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Samir with Redwood Inference, this is Lina our solutions engineer, and excited to walk through the hosted API for chat and text generation basics. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Karen: Good, thanks. We have about 45 minutes, we want to see end-to-end dev experience and understand cost/latency tradeoffs.
[00:18] Lina: Great - we'll demo streaming, common params like temperature, top_p, max_tokens, and talk about retries and backoff. We'll also show some console bits and point to the SDK. If at any point shout out questions.
[00:30] Miguel: Quick ask - we run a real-time approvals flow; latency 100-200ms per token matters. Also we have payloads with proprietary PII, so we need to understand data retention and KMS.
[00:45] Lina: Noted. We'll hit security after the demo. For latency, we'll show typical p99s and how model selection/batching affects that.

[02:15] Lina: (screen share) Ok starting with a simple chat request using the JS SDK. Code snippet: client.chat.create({model: "redwood-chat-1", messages: [...], stream: true, temperature: 0.2, max_tokens: 150}) - when stream is true we open a chunked response over Server-Sent Events, you can render tokens as they arrive.
[03:00] Karen: Is streaming SSE only or do you support websocket/HTTP2?
[03:05] Lina: Primarily SSE and HTTP chunked streaming for the hosted API today, websocket support is on the roadmap for session-based scenarios. We also have a fallback non-streaming response. Sometimes SSE can be flaky in older load balancers; we document recommended client libraries.

[05:30] Miguel: When would we use higher temperature vs top_p? We saw weird hallucinations at higher temps.
[05:38] Lina: Good question. Temperature controls randomness - 0.0 is deterministic; 0.2-0.5 is typical for assistant-style responses. top_p does nucleus sampling - we recommend tuning one at a time, often temperature=0.2 + top_p=0.9 is a good start. Also max_tokens controls length to keep latency/cost bound.

[08:00] Samir: On retries - we suggest idempotency keys for messages (we pass client_request_id) and an exponential backoff with jitter. Our SDK automatically retries safe errors (502/503/504) up to 3 times by default with base backoff 200ms. Lina, did you want to show the retry snippet?
[08:18] Lina: Yep. (paste) const res = await client.chat.create({..., retry: {maxAttempts:3, baseDelayMs:200}}) - you can override per-call. For streaming we have slightly different semantics: if connection drops you can resume via a session token for some models, but for short flows we often re-issue and use idempotency.

[12:10] Rita: Any rate limit visible in the console? We have bursty traffic from mobile app.
[12:18] Samir: In the console we show per-token and per-route throughput. Hosted API has a default rate limit per account; for production we typically recommend Redwood Dedicated or rate-limit increases depending on commit. We can configure burst windows and provide quota alerts.

[15:00] Lina: Back to params - show compare: low temp high top_p vs high temp low top_p; demo chat prompts to illustrate variability. (typing) You can also pin system messages and use per-route defaults in the Console - useful to set company-wide safety/system prompt.
[17:45] Miguel: For cost calc - does Redwood charge per input+output token?
[17:49] Samir: Yes, hosted API billing is per-token (input+output) for generation and per-embedding unit for embeddings. We can share a sample pricing calc spreadsheet. For long conversations use prefix caching to reduce tokens sent if user history is static - Console/Optimize recommends caching and batching heuristics.

[20:00] Karen: On security: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs - what's included for hosted?
[20:07] Lina: Hosted supports SSO/SAML SSO for the Console, RBAC, and audit logs. For customer data we have configurable retention; by default we retain request metadata for X days, but for enterprise plans we can set zero-retention and integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping. We'll send the SOC2 and ISO docs after the call. Note: for regulated PHI workloads we often recommend Private deployment but some customers use hosted with strict retention and encryption.

[24:30] Miguel: How deterministic are responses across variants? We may want a cheaper quantized variant in fallback.
[24:36] Lina: We have verified model variants with performance profiles - you can route by latency/cost policy. For example pay-for-latency model vs quantized cheaper variant; Redwood can automatically fallback to a compatible variant if top-tier capacity is saturated. There can be slight quality differences; Optimize gives quantization recommendations by workload.

[28:00] Samir: Let's talk about end-to-end sample benchmark - Lina prepared a simple harness. (shares link) This script runs n requests, measures p50/p90/p99 latency and token cost. We typically run customer payloads to match QPS.
[28:25] Miguel: Perfect - we'll share 3 sample payloads and our target QPS (200 reqs/sec peak) and tail requirement.

[31:10] Karen: If we start a trial, how quickly can we scale?
[31:15] Samir: Trial keys give hosted access right away; for production scale we recommend Dedicated pools with reserved capacity - can be provisioned in days for modest sizes, weeks for large capacity with procurement. We'll include options in the pricing.

[34:00] Lina: Edge cases - streaming interruptions, for mobile we recommend smaller chunk sizes and client-side aggregation to avoid flicker. Also for retries on streaming, be careful to dedupe tokens if you re-issue a request. Our SDK helps but you should test with your UI.

[37:20] Rita: Any compliance for payment data? We handle tokens and card metadata; we cannot send full PANs to third parties.
[37:30] Lina: Understood. For card data we recommend tokenization prior to sending and strict retention policies; also ROI to consider Private deployment if you need air-gapped or self-hosted option. We'll get security engaged if you want a deeper review.

[40:00] Samir: Ok recap of next steps: we'll send pricing + SOC2/ISO and demo recording, Lina will send benchmark harness and streaming example code, Miguel will share payloads and QPS. Plan POC scoping call next week. Anything else?
[40:25] Karen: No that's good. Thanks for a clear demo.
[40:30] Miguel: Thanks.
[40:33] Samir: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email.
